messages.subject: collapse() to triangle and align node label to edge of triangle
messages.subject_clean: collapse() to triangle and align node label to edge of triangle
messages.body_plain:
Hi group members,

I have been trying to collapse over 100 species OTUs in tree and then label them so that the label aligns with the edge of the triangle, but this is not done automatically with geom_nodelab() as it uses the x coordinate of the collapsed node to position the label. When there is a triangle it would be nicer to have the label at the edge of the triangle.

The only way I have been able to label the collapsed triangle at its edge is to get the x values directly from the polygon layer for each collapsed node and use geom_cladelabel() and "offset"

Is there a more automated way to plot labels of collapsed triangle nodes? It would be great to also account for whether the triangle is plotted with diffrent modes ("max", "min", "mixed")

Thanks

Peter

example below:

library(ggtree)
nwk <- system.file("extdata", "sample.nwk", package="treeio")
tree <- read.tree(nwk)
p <- ggtree(tree) + geom_tiplab()
p

# collapse nodes
collapse(p, 21, 'max', fill='steelblue',clade_name = "Clade 1", alpha=.4) %>%
  collapse(23, 'min', fill='firebrick',clade_name = "Clade 2", color='blue') -> p2

# plot collapsed node labels - do not align - have tried using nudge_x, but it is not precise
p2 + geom_nodelab()

# only way to get correct position at end of triangle is to get it directly from the polygon layer use offset through geom_cladelabel
p2 + geom_cladelabel(21, "Clade 1", offset = max(p2$layers[[4]]$data$x) - min(p2$layers[[4]]$data$x)) + geom_cladelabel(23, "Clade 2", offset = max(p2$layers[[5]]$data$x) - min(p2$layers[[5]]$data$x)) + xlim(0, 60)

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
The key is to use color gradients can be continuous variables
BTW: Welcome to talk in the groups, so that other people with the same problem can see the results of our exchange.

Here is an example. The email attachment is tree.mcc.

library(ggtree)
library(treeio)
library(ggplot2)

## import mcc tree
tree <- read.beast("tree.mcc")

## convert the tree to a tbl_tree
tree_data <- as_tibble(tree)

## have a look at location, they are discrete
## variables. We need to first replace these discrete
## variables with continuous variables.
head(tree_data$location,6)

## save oringinal discrete variables
location_s <- tree_data$location

## discrete var can be converted to numerical value by as.factor and as.numetic
## as.factor(location_s)
## > Levels: Fujian Guangdong Guangxi Hebei Henan HongKong Hunan

## to the numerical value
## The locations shown by the numbers here is consistent with the order of levels above
## Hong Kong is the 6th in levels. 6 is HongKong
location_c <- as.numeric(as.factor(location_s))

## Return numeric location to tree
tree_data$location <- location_c

## convert tbl_tree to treedata object
tree_c <- as.treedata(tree_data)

## There are 7 locations, we prepare 7 color
colors <- rainbow(7)
## name color with continue name
names(colors) <- c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7")

## set continuous = TRUE and use a continue color scale
## and meaningless continuous legend is removed
tree_plot <- ggtree(tree_c, aes(color=location), size=1.5, continuous = TRUE) +
  scale_color_gradientn(colours=colors) +
  theme(legend.position="none")

## bar plot data
x <- as.data.frame(table(location_s))
x$prop <- prop.table(x$Freq)

# rename colors with discrete name
names(colors) <- levels(as.factor(location_s))

## bar plot
bar_plot <- ggplot(data = x, aes(x = location_s, y = prop, color=NULL, fill = location_s)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
  theme(
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = NA),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = NA),
    axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black", size = 0.1),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "gray85", size = 0.05, linetype = "dotted"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = NA),
    axis.text = element_text( colour = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black", angle = 45),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA)) +
    labs(x = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL)

## create a grid plot
library(grid)

# Extract the legend
legend <- cowplot::get_legend(bar_plot)

## save to pdf
pdf("plot.pdf", paper = "a4r")
print(tree_plot)
vp <- viewport(width = 0.58, height = 0.8, x=.29, y=0.59)
pushViewport(vp)
# legend should not show in this way
print(bar_plot + theme(legend.position = "none"),vp=vp)
vp2 <- viewport(width = 0.58, height = 0.7, x=1.5, y=0)
pushViewport(vp2)
print(grid.draw(legend),vp=vp2)
dev.off()

messages.subject: colouring collapsed clades with heatmaps
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I would like to use ggtree to produce a phylogenetic tree that has:
- tips coloured by a sample type.
- nodes corresponded to multilocus genotypes reduced in size and collapsed.
- continuous traits mapped onto the tree in the form of a heatmap, where average values are calculated for the collapsed clades.

To figure out how to do this I have been working with an example dataset and my script is attached "plot_traits_example.R".

The steps in the script are as follows and plots are in the attached image:
-  create tree, multilocus genotype (mlg), sample type, and continuous trait data.
-  for the samples in the multilocus genotypes, I calculate the mean trait values.
- create ggtree object (plot A).
- rescale multilocus genotypes clades (plot B).
- collapse multilocus genotypes, note fill matches tip point colours (plot C).
- add continuous trait data to plot as a heatmap (plots D-F).

I have got an example dataset working, but when I am mapping the continuous trait data onto the tree, I lose the fill colour on the collapsed clades when I add more than two traits onto the tree, and I cannot figure why this is happening.

See attached image and compare the collapsed clades in plots E and F.

I presume this is because the colour scale is overridden somehow? Can new_scale_fill() only be used a set number of times?

I hope this makes sense, the code should work out of the box, and I would appreciate and advice or feedback.

Best wishes
Ollie

Alright, well here's a reproducible example ^_^:

This is a trait that I mapped onto the tree and used "make.simmap" from "phylotools" for ancestral character reconstruction:

AcetylTrait <- setNames(OccupMatrix$Acetyl, OccupMatrix$Species)
AcetylTrait<- as.factor(AcetylTrait)
cols<-setNames(c("darkorange1","blue"), levels(AcetylTrait))
mtree<-make.simmap(BigProk.Tree,AcetylTrait,model="ER")
plot(mtree,cols,type="phylogram",ftype="off", lwd=0.4)

The tree and characters are plotting very well, like this:

Now, I have another tree that I want to compare to this one using the example that you provided here: http://yulab-smu.top/treedata-book/chapter2.html#ggtree-fortify (Figure 2.6)

Code used for the second tree:

nwk <- system.file("extdata", "AcetylTree.nwk", package="treeio")
Acetyl.Tree <- read.tree(nwk)
Acetyl.df<-arrange(as_tibble(Acetyl.Tree), desc(label))

metadata<-read.csv("Acetyl.csv", sep=";", header = TRUE)
Phyla<-c(metadata$lv2_group)
length(Phyla)<-length(Acetyl.df$label)
Acetyl.df.1<-tibble(Acetyl.df, Phyla)
grp<-tapply(Acetyl.df.1$label, Acetyl.df.1$Phyla, list)
AcetylTree<-groupOTU(Acetyl.Tree, grp, 'Phyla')

p<-ggtree(AcetylTree, aes(color=Phyla), ladderize=FALSE, size=0.2) +
  theme(legend.position="right") +
  geom_tiplab(size=1, color="gray30") +
  geom_rootedge(rootedge = 0.01, color ="tan") +
  geom_nodelab(size=1, color="brown") +
  geom_nodepoint(size=0.1) +
  geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=node), size=0.1)

p

Libraries used:
library("treeio")
library("ggtree")
library("ape")
library("tidytree")
library("tibble")
library("ggplot2")
library("phytools")

R version: R version 4.0.2 (2020-06-22). RStudio version: 1.3.1073

Ggtree is a terrific package!

messages.body_plain:
I have checked your example code, and there are indeed some errors that are not convenient for us to help you solve the problem.
BigProk.Tree has not been assigned, we have no way of getting it.

For example, ggtree can plot SIMMAP tree like this.
http://yulab-smu.top/treedata-book/chapter8.html#subplots 8.3.1 Annotate with bar charts
anoletree is an example SIMMAP tree in phytools.

Of course, you need to use the read.simmap function in phytools to import your tree file firstly, and then use ggtree for visualization.
As already said here https://groups.google.com/g/bioc-ggtree/c/wP6dJHYst5U/m/l0HnkUfIBgAJ

After you get two ggtree objects,
Finally, you can use the method here to complete the comparison https://groups.google.com/g/bioc-ggtree/c/JvxDE3OdLxk/m/D8SU419BBwAJ

Therefore, it is very important to import your tree. But you seem to have a problem at this step. https://groups.google.com/g/bioc-ggtree/c/wP6dJHYst5U/m/GBHRYd_oBgAJ
That is the reason why I asked you for an example SIMMAP tree.

At last,
I am very disappointed in your conversation with the developer above.
First of all, you did not check and correct your mistakes after the developer reminded you.
Second, you used Google's word meaning as a reply, which is an offensive behavior.
I don't care what difficulties you encounter when understanding and solving problems, how upset you are,
but respecting developers, especially developers who kindly help you solve problems, is what you should do.
Please be patient and respectful.
No matter how much you have done, are doing for yourself,
and the developer is taking the time to help you solve the problem,
if not pregnant with a thankful heart, so please do not offend.
